_doc: What forge needs from Claude Code, declared rather than assumed.
forge writes hooks, permission rules and a statusline into ~/.claude and
then depends on Claude Code to honour them. Every one of those is an
undocumented coupling until it is written down here. This has already bitten
twice: a removed `claude plugins add` verb made install silently install zero
plugins and report success, and an `if:` filter written at the wrong nesting
level was discarded for three releases while the notes claimed a 95-99%
min_claude_code is a hard floor — install refuses below it.
tested_claude_code is the version this was last verified against; above it
forge warns but proceeds, because refusing to run on a newer Claude Code
would be worse than the risk.

if._doc: MUST be on the individual hook object, not the matcher group. The group schema is {matcher?, hooks[]} and unknown keys are stripped, so a misplaced `if` fails silently rather than erroring.

permissions.deny._doc: Needed by the permissions v2 work. Not yet written by forge.

permissions.ask._doc: Needed by the permissions v2 work. Not yet written by forge.

sandbox._doc: Not yet written by forge. Gated behind its own decision.

_doc: Behaviour forge relies on but has NOT confirmed by execution. Each needs a
live check before anything is built on top of it. Listed here so the
assumption is visible rather than buried in a comment.
unverified.bash_find_covers_exec: Does Bash(find:*) also permit `find -exec` and `find -delete`? Decides whether the read-only preset tier is genuinely read-only.
unverified.bash_wrapper_stripping: Which wrapper commands the matcher strips before matching (timeout, nice, xargs, env...). Determines which allow-list entries are inert.
unverified.rule_precedence_under_bypass: deny is reportedly ignored under bypassPermissions while ask still prompts. If true, anything that must hold in bypass mode belongs in ask, not deny.
